title: Desk Training Q&A: Buyer Closing Moves and Builder Extended Rate Lock Extensions
content:
**Q: Do the buyer's own requests to move closing count when a Builder Extended Rate Lock is extended?**
A: Yes. A purchase agreement with two or more buyer-requested closing extensions written adds 3 days to the days to cover; one written adds 1 day; none adds none. The days are added before the days to cover are rounded up to whole increments.

**Q: Where is the count read?**
A: From the Home Purchase Agreement record the lock finances — the number of buyer-requested closing extensions written on the agreement.

**Q: How does the count map to days?**
A:

| Buyer-requested closing extensions written on the Home Purchase Agreement | Days added |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 3 |
| 3 or more | 3 |

**Q: A buyer has three closing extensions written. Does the third add more?**
A: No. Two or more written add 3 days in total.

**Q (hypothetical figures): 13 days to cover on a lock with 7-day increments and one buyer-requested closing extension written — how many increments?**
A: 13 plus 1 is 14 days, which is exactly 2 increments.
